message.content: **Summary:** I read Walmart's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-01-31) and the picture was positive: the business grew and converted earnings strongly into cash. Because the narrative in the filing text quoted total net sales of $648,125M, I cross-checked every figure with the trusted SEC lookup and used the reported values — revenue $642,637M (vs. $611,289M the prior year, ~5% growth), operating income $27,012M (up sharply from $20,428M), net income $15,511M (vs. $11,680M), diluted EPS $1.91 (vs. $1.42), and operating cash flow $35,726M — with management also stating liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months. With WMT quoted at $69.96 (bid $69.94 / ask $69.98), I placed a single limit buy order for 70 shares at $70.00, which filled at $70.00 for about $4,900 — inside the $5,000 per-order cap, well within the $10,000 daily total, at a price essentially at market, and with no money leaving the account (cash was ~$50,000, plus 100 NVDA shares already held). No NVDA trades were made, so the full $10,000 daily budget wasn't needed; the $5,100 remaining capacity is left unused unless you want to add.
message.reasoning: Order filled at $70.00, 70 shares = $4,900. Total today: $4,900 ≤ $10,000. Write summary.
